effective.basis: TCG release of the first printing carrying the errata'd text (LCJW-EN271, Legendary Collection 4: Joey's World Mega Pack)

changes.historical_text: Once this turn, negate 1 six-sided die roll and re-roll it.
changes.modern_text: One time, during the rest of this turn, if either player(s) rolls a die (or dice), you can have the player(s) re-roll. (You can only gain this effect once per turn.)
changes.summary: Functional erratum: LCJW-EN271 adds the rider '(You can only gain this effect once per turn.)', which no earlier printing carries - under 'Once this turn, negate 1 six-sided die roll and re-roll it' each copy grants its own re-roll, so two copies activated in the same turn give two re-rolls, while the errata'd card grants nothing for the second copy. The same printing also widens the scope from '1 six-sided die roll' to any roll of 'a die (or dice)' by either player and drops the negation framing in favour of 'you can have the player(s) re-roll'.

gap.reason: Project Ignis ships no historical implementation of this card; reproducing the era behaviour needs a custom script and a reserved passcode
gap.behavioural_impact: In GOAT and Edison, two copies of Dice Re-Roll activated in one turn should buy two re-rolls, and the effect is written for a six-sided die roll only; the shipped card grants the re-roll effect once per turn no matter how many copies are activated and applies to any die or dice.

review.notes: upstream_implementations is empty. Chain starts at v1 (DR1-EN262, 2005-03-19), the text in force at the 2005-04-01 GOAT snapshot (Dark Revelation Volume 1 released thirteen days earlier) and still the current text at the 2010-04-24 Edison snapshot, since the next printing is LCJW-EN271 on 2013-10-11. Pre-baseline v0 (DCR-100, 2003-12-01) says the same thing at greater length ('After this card is activated, for the rest of this turn you can negate 1 six-sided die roll and re-roll it') and is behaviourally identical to v1. v2 is the pinned cdb text. The functional call rests on the added parenthetical, which is a per-turn cap on gaining the effect rather than on using it - the era text caps uses per copy, not per turn. No entry for this card in edison-functional-errata.md.
